claim_review_spans.R1: You spent nearly a week on this paper, then got a mark far below what you were used to. That hurts—and it makes sense that starting another paper now feels intimidating.
claim_review_spans.R2: **You’re not wrong to consider dropping the class. But I wouldn’t agree that it’s the only sensible option, or that this mark proves you can’t do university in English.** The feedback points to a particular writing expectation, not a verdict on your ability. You don’t have to decide about dropping while you’re also unsure which assignment is due.
claim_review_spans.R3: “Your own argument” usually means **your answer to the assignment’s question, supported by reasons and evidence**. Changing words from a reading is paraphrasing: the wording may be yours, but the idea still comes from the source and generally needs a citation. That’s a distinction you can learn—not something you should automatically have known.
claim_review_spans.R4: - **Argument:** “Universities should subsidize student transport because access to classes depends partly on affordable travel.” You would then use readings as evidence and explain how they support your claim.
claim_review_spans.R5: **For now, do just one thing: identify the assignment page.** Look at the course name or code at the top, then open that course’s assignment list to check the title and deadline. You don’t need to write a sentence yet.
claim_review_spans.R6: > Hi, I’m seeing an assignment titled “[title]” with a deadline of tomorrow at 5 p.m., but I had understood the next paper was due in two weeks. Could you confirm whether this is the next assignment for [course]? I’m concerned I may have mixed up my course pages.
claim_review_spans.R7: Before actually dropping, confirm the academic and any immigration-status consequences with your academic adviser and international student office; those depend on your circumstances.
claim_review_spans.R8: No questionnaire from me. **First, establish what is due. The decision about the class can be considered separately from what this painful mark is telling you about yourself.**
